Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue "ObjectSizeTests.cs uses `#if NET462 || NET` but NET462 is not defined" (#2147) at dotnet/Open-XML-SDK
Events.RelatedBody:
**Describe the bug**
The test file ObjectSizeTests.cs uses `#if NET462 || NET`  but I don't see NET462 defined. Should it be `NET462_OR_GREATER || NET` or just `NET472 || NET` (given net462 isn't a valid compile target for this library) or just remove the conditional entirely?, so it can run on NET472 ?

https://github.com/dotnet/Open-XML-SDK/blob/431ab05cf160248cc3885a4a766026d4f8243792/test/DocumentFormat.OpenXml.Framework.Tests/ObjectSizeTests.cs#L4

Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue "Provide a way to describe the root element of a VML part" (#2145) at dotnet/Open-XML-SDK
Events.RelatedBody:
The SDK provides classes which map to VML elements, but there does not seem a way to describe the **root element** of a VML drawing part. Unlike other kinds of parts it is a simply named `<xml>`.

Moreover, I tried loading a XLSX file containing a VML part (in particular a picture in the document heading), but the `RootElement` of the `VmlDrawingPart` is null:

```csharp
using DocumentFormat.OpenXml.Packaging;
using System.Linq;

using var document = SpreadsheetDocument.Open(@"c:\path\to\file.xlsx", true);
var vmlRoot = document.WorkbookPart.WorksheetParts.SelectMany(d => d.VmlDrawingParts).FirstOrDefault(p => p != null)?.RootElement; // is null
```

I know VML is a legacy format, but since it is still apparently in use there should be a way to handle it via the SDK.

Some cases I found:
- pictures in the header / footer of a XLSX document
- comments in a XLSX document (see also https://github.com/dotnet/Open-XML-SDK/issues/1549)
